title: Unified error intake proxy and OLAP dashboard for throttles & model rejects
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Production alerts surface spikes in 5xxs and user-facing timeouts, but signals are fragmented across HTTP proxies, model-serving logs, and distributed traces. Current dashboards duplicate counts (proxy + runtime) and lack a normalized taxonomy to drive reliable routing/fallback policies.

Goal: Build an error intake proxy and normalization pipeline that: (1) ingests HTTP/gRPC responses, model server error records, and tracing hooks; (2) applies a deterministic failure taxonomy (timeout, overload, model_reject, invalid_input, auth, upstream_503, client_cancel); (3) enriches records with trace_id, route/model_version, queue length and GPU utilization snapshot; (4) writes deduplicated canonical error rows to an OLAP store and materialized views used by a new error dashboard and SLO impact reports.

Scope: Implementation includes a lightweight sidecar intake (K8s DaemonSet) for Dedicated & Private, a hosted intake lambda for Redwood API, normalization rules, enrichment joiners for trace sampling events, ClickHouse schema and materialized views, a Metabase dashboard (or Looker tile) with prebuilt slices for error class trends, latency histograms by error class, and a runbook mapping taxonomy -> remediation/playbook.

Out of scope: Long-term ML-based error classifier (future follow-up), automated rollback actions (ops will be manual for initial rollout).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical error row schema defined and reviewed by Observability and Runtime teams
Intake proxy deployed in staging ingesting HTTP/gRPC and model error events with trace hook enrichment
De-duplication logic works end-to-end: single user request that surfaces proxy and runtime errors produces one canonical record
ClickHouse materialized views populated within SLAs (<= 30s eventual), and queries for common slices complete < 2s
Metabase dashboard with: error-class time-series, top routes by error-rate, latency distribution per error-class, and SLO exposure widget is available
Runbook documenting taxonomy, alert thresholds, and owner for each failure class is published
Telemetry-backed smoke tests demonstrate reduction in false-positive incident noise by >= 40% (compared to baseline)
comments: 2025-02-16 Ramon Garcia: Spike week — prototyped intake sidecar that attaches trace_id from X-Request-ID. Needs robust sampling guard to avoid overload. Next: add queue_length and gpu_load enrichment hooks.

2025-02-20 Aisha Patel: Architecture review done. Decision: use ClickHouse for OLAP store and Kafka as durable buffer. Security: encrypted topics + schema registry. Action: prod security review scheduled.

2025-02-24 SRE (review): Concern about intake creating additional tail latency. Proposed mitigation: async fire-and-forget to Kafka with local batching and backpressure shed to preserve client latency.
2025-02-27 Ramon Garcia: Implemented de-dup key (trace_id + canonical_error_class + route + minute_bucket). Integration tests show dedupe rate ~92% on sampled test workload.
2025-03-01 UX: Dashboard v1 reviewed — requested adding a per-tenant filter and a compact SLO exposure card. Agree to add in follow-up sprint.
2025-03-02 Aisha Patel: Security review completed (ticket sec-OBS-88). Approvals: SRE, Security, Product. Plan: deploy to staging next week; monitor error ingress QPS and consumer lag.
implementation_notes: Normalization rules: map HTTP 504 -> timeout; gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED -> timeout; 429/HTTP_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS -> overload; model 4xx validation -> invalid_input; model 5xx with 'OOM' or 'no_memory' -> model_resource_exhaustion; rejections with 'token_limit' -> model_truncation_reject
Trace hook: add trace-span tagging for 'error_class' in runtime before surfacing to intake. Use OpenTelemetry semantic conventions where possible.
Backfill plan: run a one-time mapping job over last 7 days of logs to bootstrap dashboards; mark backfill rows with 'inferred_from_logs' flag.
Alerting: new Alert policy 'error-class surge' will fire when any canonical class exceeds baseline + 3 sigma for 5m for top-5 customer routes.
Rollout: Canary in staging -> Canary in prod (1%) -> Prod ramp (10/30/100%) with circuit-breaker to stop ingest if downstream lags exceed 60s.
